refresh_note: Every read-only evidence command in this file was re-run unprivileged on 2026-09-28, and each toolchain row was re-read with the tool's own version command. One command was not repeated: the virt-fw-vars command of capabilities.secure_boot_enrolment writes a variable store and carries <guid> placeholders, so its guest_enrolment_proven reading stands from 2026-09-13 (D62) and that row's recorded_on covers its host-firmware text only. A row whose reading changed carries recorded_on 2026-09-28 and states what it read before; a row first recorded that day carries the same date; a row without its own recorded_on read the same on both dates. The kernel block is the one exception and says why.
evidence_class: Development evidence only. A check that passes on this profile does not qualify hardware, does not close a blocked gate, and is not release evidence. Hardware qualification needs more than one machine and the acceptance recorded in the milestone.

kernel.reread_note: The same evidence command on 2026-09-28 printed 7.2.8-1-cachyos and read every symbol in config in the state recorded here. release stays the 2026-09-13 reading because build/kernel-requirement.reference.json pins its module ABI to it, M18 recorded its evidence against it, and the M19 BPF gate names it as REFERENCE_PROFILE_KERNEL. realtime_kernel.note: the running kernel is PREEMPT_DYNAMIC, and this stays present:false because it is a reading of the HOST. The distribution ships linux-rt 7.2.8.rt3.arch1-1 (7.2.5.rt3.arch1-1 on 2026-09-13), which would be an operator action rather than a missing capability; milestone M23 did not take it. It boots the kernel this repository builds in M26 (CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT=y, release 7.2.5-aegis-m26) as a guest kernel instead, so a realtime measurement was obtained with no installation and no bootloader entry (D57, D70). The negative half of that fixture depends on this row staying false, and `make verify-latency` re-reads both kernels with one probe on every run

secure_boot_enrolment.note: disabled in the running firmware and not enrolled on the host. Re-read 2026-09-28: the host firmware is in setup mode with no PK, KEK, db or dbx enrolled (see firmware); on 2026-09-13 it carried vendor keys with SetupMode off. No key has been enrolled on the host, and whether this firmware accepts enrolment from the running OS in setup mode has not been tried. That does not gate guest work: a variable store with platform key, KEK and db enrolled and SecureBootEnable set was generated here from the shipped OVMF_VARS with virt-fw-vars, and OVMF_CODE.secboot is installed

gpu_dma_buf_and_peer_memory.note: NVIDIA 615.71.09 open kernel modules (Dual MIT/GPL) with nvidia_drm modeset and the nvidia_peermem peer-memory module installed, CUDA 13.4.2 present (13.3.1 on 2026-09-13); the Intel and AMD cards provide DMA-BUF through their in-tree drivers; the Arc A380 is bound to i915 at probe time, and the same kernel ships xe with a PCI alias for 8086:56a5 (CONFIG_DRM_XE=m), so rebinding it to xe for drm_sched is supported here

vaapi_decode.evidence_command: LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD vainfo --display drm --device /dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000:03:00.0-render; vainfo --display drm --device /dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000:03:00.0-render; env -u LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME vainfo --display drm --device /dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000:03:00.0-render; readlink -f /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:03:00.0/driver; ls -l /dev/dri/by-path; cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:03:00.0/vendor /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:03:00.0/device; pacman -Q libva intel-media-driver
vaapi_decode.observed: with LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD: 'Intel iHD driver for Intel(R) Gen Graphics - 26.2.4' on the Arc A380 (8086:56a5, i915, /dev/dri/by-path/pci-0000:03:00.0-render -> renderD129), listing VAEntrypointVLD for VAProfileMPEG2Main, VAProfileJPEGBaseline, VAProfileH264High, VAProfileHEVCMain, VAProfileVP9Profile0 and VAProfileAV1Profile0, and VAEntrypointVideoProc; banner 'VA-API version: 1.24 (libva 2.24.0)' from package libva 2.24.1-1.1. With the session's LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia the same call on the same node reports 'VA-API NVDEC driver [direct backend]'; with the variable unset it reports the iHD driver 26.2.4. The sysfs vendor and device files read 0x8086 and 0x56a5, and pacman -Q reports libva 2.24.1-1.1 and intel-media-driver 26.2.4-1.1
vaapi_decode.note: the driver must be pinned per run: /etc/environment.d/85-nvidia-vaapi.conf sets LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia for the session, and the call above that inherits the session environment loads the NVIDIA driver even when the Intel render node is named. renderD numbers follow probe order, and the PCI path is the stable name. This row records what the driver advertises; no committed gate has decoded a frame (M27)

wayland_layer_shell.observed: interface zwlr_layer_shell_v1 version 5, advertised by the host session compositor, kwin 6.7.5 (package kwin 6.7.5-1.1)
wayland_layer_shell.note: this is the host desktop session's compositor, not P04 aegis-compositor, which serves no Wayland protocol; a run against it is development evidence for the client half only (D79). kwin_wayland --version and pacman -Q report the installed kwin, not which process served the session socket; that the session compositor is that kwin is inferred. M27's gate (run r20260929T151938-0d35) read the session socket's peer with SO_PEERCRED: /usr/bin/kwin_wayland_wrapper (pid 3089, package kwin 6.7.5-1.1), which holds the listening socket for kwin_wayland
